categories.name: Coding Agents & AI IDEs

tools.name: Cursor
tools.use: AI-first code editor for building and refactoring whole apps
tools.why: A code editor with AI built in. You type what you want changed and it edits your project for you.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.use: Terminal-based agent for multi-file changes in real repos
tools.why: Give it a task in plain English and it reads your whole project and makes the changes itself.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.use: Inline completions and agent mode inside VS Code and GitHub
tools.why: Suggests the next lines of code as you type, so it's a gentle way to start using AI for coding.

tools.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
tools.use: Agentic IDE for running and managing local and cloud coding agents
tools.why: An AI code editor that can take on bigger multi-step jobs across your project with little hand-holding.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.use: Delegating coding tasks to a cloud or CLI agent
tools.why: ChatGPT's coding agent. Hand it a job and it works through it in the background.

categories.beginner: An AI helper that writes and fixes code with you, like a programmer sitting next to you who never gets tired.

categories.name: App Builders

tools.name: Lovable
tools.use: Prompt-to-full-stack web app with Supabase integration
tools.why: Easiest place to start: describe your app and it builds a working version you can click around in minutes.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.use: In-browser prompt-to-app builds you can run and deploy
tools.why: Type an idea and get a working website or app right in your browser, nothing to install.

tools.name: v0
tools.use: Generating React/Next.js UI and apps from prompts
tools.why: Great for good-looking websites and pages. Describe the look and it builds it for you.

tools.name: Replit
tools.use: Cloud IDE with an agent that builds and hosts apps
tools.why: Build, run and publish an app all in one place in your browser, with an AI helper that does the coding.

categories.beginner: Describe what you want in plain English and these build a working app or website for you, no coding needed to start.

categories.name: Deploy & Hosting

tools.name: Vercel
tools.use: Deploying Next.js and frontend apps from Git
tools.why: One click to put your website online with a real link, and it's free for small sites.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.use: Static sites and Jamstack apps with simple deploys
tools.why: Drag and drop your site to get it live on the internet. Simple and free to start.

tools.name: Cloudflare Pages
tools.use: Fast global static hosting plus Workers for edge logic
tools.why: Free, fast hosting for websites, backed by one of the biggest internet companies.

tools.name: Railway
tools.use: Deploying backends, workers, and databases with little config
tools.why: Puts apps that need a server or database online without you managing any computers.

tools.name: Render
tools.use: Hosting web services, cron jobs, and Postgres
tools.why: A simple place to run your app and its database online, with a free tier to try it.

categories.beginner: Where your website or app lives on the internet so anyone can visit it with a link.

categories.name: Auth

tools.name: Clerk
tools.use: Drop-in sign-in UI and user management for React/Next.js
tools.why: Adds polished sign-up and log-in screens to your app in minutes.

tools.name: Supabase Auth
tools.use: Auth bundled with your Supabase Postgres database
tools.why: Free log-ins that come bundled with Supabase, so your accounts and data live in one place.

tools.name: Auth0
tools.use: Enterprise-grade auth, SSO, and identity
tools.why: Battle-tested log-in system that big companies trust when security really matters.

tools.name: Firebase Authentication
tools.use: Simple auth for mobile and web apps on Google's stack
tools.why: Google's free log-in system, with easy 'Sign in with Google' and phone login.

categories.beginner: Handles sign-up, log-in and passwords so your users can have accounts without you building it from scratch.

categories.name: Databases & Backend

tools.name: Supabase
tools.use: Postgres, auth, storage, and realtime in one backend
tools.why: Stores your app's data plus log-ins and file uploads, all in one free-to-start package.

tools.name: Firebase
tools.use: Realtime NoSQL backend for quick mobile/web apps
tools.why: Google's all-in-one backend for saving data, great for phone apps and realtime updates.

tools.name: Neon
tools.use: Serverless Postgres with branching
tools.why: A simple online database that's free to start and only charges when it's actually being used.

tools.name: Convex
tools.use: Reactive TypeScript backend with built-in database
tools.why: A backend where your app's data updates live on screen, without setting up servers.

tools.name: PlanetScale
tools.use: Scalable managed MySQL/Postgres
tools.why: A heavy-duty database for when your app gets lots of users and needs to stay fast.

categories.beginner: The place your app saves its information, like customers, orders or jobs, so nothing gets lost.

categories.name: Design-to-Code

tools.name: Figma Make
tools.use: Turning prompts and Figma designs into working prototypes
tools.why: Sketch or describe a screen and it turns it into a working prototype you can click.

tools.name: Builder.io
tools.use: Converting Figma designs into framework code
tools.why: Turns designs into real web pages and lets you edit the site visually, like a page builder.

tools.name: Locofy
tools.use: Figma/Penpot to React, Next.js, and mobile code
tools.why: Converts your Figma designs into real app or website code.

tools.name: Anima
tools.use: Exporting Figma designs to React/HTML code
tools.why: Takes a design from Figma and turns it into a working website.

categories.beginner: Turns a picture or mockup of how your app should look into a real, clickable screen.

categories.name: Testing & QA

tools.name: Playwright
tools.use: Reliable end-to-end browser tests (open source)
tools.why: Free tool that clicks through your site like a real person to catch anything that breaks.

tools.name: Cypress
tools.use: Developer-friendly E2E and component testing
tools.why: Lets you watch automated tests click through your app so you can see exactly where bugs happen.

tools.name: Sentry
tools.use: Catching errors and crashes in production
tools.why: Emails you when your live app crashes and shows exactly what went wrong.

tools.name: CodeRabbit
tools.use: AI code review on pull requests
tools.why: An AI reviewer that reads your code changes and points out bugs before they go live.

categories.beginner: Tools that check your app for bugs and broken buttons before your customers find them.

categories.name: LLM APIs

tools.name: OpenAI API
tools.use: General-purpose GPT models for chat, tools, and vision
tools.why: The ChatGPT brain you can plug into your own app or chatbot.

tools.name: Anthropic API
tools.use: Claude models, strong at coding and long context
tools.why: Claude's brain for your own app. Great at writing, reasoning and long documents.

tools.name: Google Gemini API
tools.use: Gemini models with large context and multimodal input
tools.why: Google's AI with a generous free tier, good for chatbots and reading images or PDFs.

tools.name: xAI API
tools.use: Grok models via an OpenAI-compatible API
tools.why: Grok's AI for your own app, with up-to-date knowledge and a big memory for long chats.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.use: One API key to route across many model providers
tools.why: One account to try many different AI models and pick the best price for your chatbot.

categories.beginner: The AI 'brains' you plug into your own app to make it chat, write, answer questions or read documents.

categories.name: AI Images & Art
categories.beginner: Tools that make pictures from a sentence you type. Describe what you want, like "a cute cartoon cat emote waving", and they draw it in seconds. Great for emotes, stickers, logos, thumbnails, avatars and art for games.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.use: Logos, stickers, posters and images with readable text
tools.why: The best at putting real, readable words inside a picture, so it's great for logos, thumbnails and channel art. Free credits every week.

tools.name: Leonardo
tools.use: Emotes, game assets, characters and stylized art
tools.why: Lots of ready-made art styles for cartoons, game items and characters, which makes it easy to get a consistent look for a set of emotes. Free tokens every day.

tools.name: ChatGPT Images
tools.use: Quick images and edits by chatting
tools.why: Just describe the picture in plain English and ask for changes like "make it smaller and add a blue outline". Easiest place to start.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.use: Logos, icons, vector art and brand sets
tools.why: Makes clean logos and icons that stay sharp at any size, so they look good as tiny emotes and on big banners alike.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.use: High-quality illustrations and artistic images
tools.why: Produces some of the most beautiful, artistic images around. No free plan, so try a free option first.

categories.name: AI Audio & Voice
categories.beginner: Tools that make sound for you. Type a description or a script and they create music, jingles, realistic voiceovers, or clean up and transcribe your recordings. Great for podcasts, YouTube and stream intros.

tools.name: Suno
tools.use: Songs, jingles and background music from a text description
tools.why: Describe the song you want, like "upbeat 10-second podcast intro jingle", and it makes it with music and even vocals. Free to try; downloading and commercial use need the $10/mo plan.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.use: Realistic AI voiceovers, narration, sound effects and music
tools.why: Paste your script and it reads it out in a natural human-sounding voice. Also makes sound effects. Free monthly credits, paid from $6/mo.

tools.name: Descript
tools.use: Edit podcasts and videos by editing the transcript
tools.why: Turns your recording into text, and you edit the audio just like a document: delete a word and it's gone from the recording. Free plan includes 60 minutes a month.

categories.name: AI for Hardware & Electronics
categories.beginner: Tools for projects you can touch: Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi boards, sensors, wiring, robots, 3D printing and smart-home gadgets. They help you write the code for your board, test your wiring safely on screen before you plug anything in, and even design your own circuit boards.

tools.name: Arduino Cloud
tools.use: Write, upload and control Arduino/ESP32 projects with a built-in AI assistant
tools.why: Arduino's own online editor has an AI helper that writes and fixes the code for your board, and lets you control wireless (Wi-Fi) projects from your phone. Free plan includes 30 AI requests a month.

tools.name: Wokwi
tools.use: Simulate Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi Pico projects in your browser
tools.why: Build and test your circuit on screen with virtual boards, sensors and LEDs, including Wi-Fi on the ESP32, so you can't fry real parts while learning. Free for public projects.

tools.name: Tinkercad
tools.use: Beginner circuits and 3D-printable designs
tools.why: Autodesk's free, super-friendly tool for designing parts to 3D print and wiring up practice circuits with a virtual Arduino.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.use: Explain wiring, write firmware and troubleshoot step by step
tools.why: Describe your parts and what you want them to do and it explains the wiring and writes the board code. You can even send it a photo of your setup when something isn't working.

tools.name: Flux
tools.use: AI-assisted circuit and PCB design
tools.why: An AI helper for designing your own custom circuit board, from parts list to a board you can order. Paid after a 14-day free trial (free for students).

tools.name: OpenPLC
tools.use: Free, open-source PLC you can program with ladder logic
tools.why: Learn and test PLC programs (ladder logic, structured text) for free without buying an industrial controller. It can run on a regular PC or a Raspberry Pi.

categories.name: AI Video & Clips
categories.beginner: Tools for short videos: TikToks, Reels, YouTube Shorts and stream highlights. They cut long videos into clips, add captions automatically and help you edit without learning pro software.

tools.name: CapCut
tools.use: Edit shorts and reels with auto captions
tools.why: A free, easy video editor made for TikTok-style videos. Auto captions, templates and simple cuts are on the free plan; some effects need Pro.

tools.name: Opus Clip
tools.use: Turn a long video or stream into short clips
tools.why: Upload a long video or paste a YouTube link and AI picks the best moments, crops them vertical and adds captions. Free plan gives 60 minutes of video a month, with a watermark.

tools.name: Descript
tools.use: Edit video by editing the transcript
tools.why: Your video becomes a text document. Delete words in the text and they're cut from the video. Good for talking videos and podcasts.

tools.name: Runway
tools.use: Generate short AI video clips from text or images
tools.why: Makes brand-new video clips from a description or a picture. Free plan is a one-time 125 credits, enough to try a few clips.

categories.name: Automations & Agents
categories.beginner: Tools that connect your apps so boring tasks happen on their own, like sending new form signups to a spreadsheet or emailing you when an order comes in. No coding needed.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.use: Connect apps with simple if-this-then-that steps
tools.why: The easiest place to start: pick a trigger and an action and it just runs. Free plan covers 100 tasks a month with two-step automations.

tools.name: Make
tools.use: Visual drag-and-drop automations
tools.why: Draw your automation as a flowchart. More free room than Zapier (1,000 credits a month), a little more to learn.

tools.name: n8n
tools.use: Powerful automations and AI agents you can host yourself
tools.why: Very flexible and free if you run it on your own computer or server. The hosted version is a 14-day trial, then paid. Best once you're comfortable.

categories.name: Websites & Stores
categories.beginner: For a simple business website or online shop, like a bakery, a portfolio or selling your crafts. These build the site for you from templates or a prompt, and you edit by dragging things around. No coding, and no need for a full custom app.

tools.name: Wix
tools.use: AI-built business websites with drag-and-drop editing
tools.why: Describe your business and its AI builds a starter site you can then drag and edit. Free plan works but shows Wix ads and a wixsite.com address.

tools.name: Shopify
tools.use: Online store to sell products
tools.why: The standard for selling things online: products, checkout, shipping and payments in one place. Short free trial, then usually $1 a month for 3 months before regular pricing.

tools.name: Framer
tools.use: Good-looking sites and landing pages with AI layouts
tools.why: Great for a sharp-looking landing page or portfolio. AI can draft the layout for you. Free plan uses a Framer address and badge.

tools.name: Squarespace
tools.use: Polished templates for a simple business site or shop
tools.why: Clean, professional templates that are hard to make look bad. No free plan, but there's a 14-day free trial.

categories.name: Writing & Marketing
categories.beginner: Tools for the words around your project: social posts, emails, newsletters, product descriptions and ads. Tell them what you sell and who it's for, then edit the draft so it sounds like you.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.use: Draft posts, emails and product descriptions
tools.why: Tell it what you're selling and who it's for and it writes a first draft in seconds. Ask for a few versions and pick the one that sounds most like you.

tools.name: Claude
tools.use: Natural-sounding writing and rewrites
tools.why: Good at writing that doesn't sound like a robot, and at rewriting your own draft to be clearer. Free plan has daily limits.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.use: Fix spelling, grammar and tone as you type
tools.why: Checks your writing everywhere you type, in email, social posts and docs. The free plan catches spelling and grammar mistakes.

categories.name: CAD & Machining
categories.beginner: Tools for designing real parts and making them on a 3D printer, CNC mill or lathe. Honest note: most CAD and CAM is not AI yet. A few tools now let you describe a part in words, and AI chat can help explain G-code, but always check toolpaths and simulate before you cut metal.

tools.name: Fusion
tools.use: CAD and CAM in one, from design to toolpaths
tools.why: Design the part and make the toolpaths in the same program. Free for personal, non-commercial use (under $1,000 a year), with limits like 10 active designs and 3-axis CAM. Its AI Assistant is still a preview, and generative design needs a paid plan.

tools.name: Onshape
tools.use: Browser-based CAD that runs on any computer
tools.why: Full 3D CAD in your web browser, no install. Free plan, but your designs are public. Includes an AI Advisor that answers how-to questions.

tools.name: Zoo Zookeeper
tools.use: Describe a part in words and get an editable 3D CAD model
tools.why: Type something like "a flange with 4 bolt holes" and it makes an editable CAD model you can export as STEP. Works best on simple parts. Free plan includes $10 of AI use a month.

tools.name: Tinkercad
tools.use: Very simple 3D designs for printing
tools.why: Autodesk's free beginner tool. Not AI, but the easiest way to make a 3D-printable part in an afternoon.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.use: Explain and draft G-code, feeds and speeds
tools.why: Good for learning what G-code lines do or drafting a simple program from your dimensions and tool. It can get things wrong, so always simulate and dry-run above the part before cutting.

releases.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 now powers the deepseek-flash API model (open weights on Hugging Face), and DeepSeek's Search and Fetch web APIs are open to all developers at $0.75 per 1,000 calls

Beam, a 501B-parameter (23B active) open-weight model for coding and agents, is out under Apache 2.0 with the open-source Mirror CLI; free to start on Reflection's API and also on OpenRouter, Vercel, Ollama and other partners
Cloud agents can now build interactive canvases (dashboards, reports) you share with a link; Environments API in beta; cloud environments now hold up to 300 repos and large ones load 5x faster
JetBrains' free on-device coding agent runs on NVIDIA RTX Spark at launch, and Windows support is now stable on RTX cards with 24 GB+ VRAM: no token bill, and your code never leaves the machine
Google AI Pro subscribers can now build apps with Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio Build and the playground
HeyGen Video 1, its video generation model, is now available in the HeyGen MCP server, so you can ask your AI agent for a video and get it back in seconds
New Agents section in your Clerk app config with setup for adding auth to your MCP server, plus a ready-made agent prompt for building a new MCP server

Code Review is generally available on Claude Team and Enterprise: automatic reviews on new GitHub pull requests, about 3x faster than the preview (6-10 minutes), with Quick, Standard or Deep review levels per repo
Fast mode for Claude Opus 5.5 is out of research preview: up to 2.5x faster output, no waitlist or beta header, $8/$40 per million tokens
Neon Realtime in public beta: subscribe to any read-only SQL query and your app updates live, with React hooks and a coding-agent skill; free during beta
Code layers enter open beta (code-backed prototypes on the canvas, all plans), plus Specs for Markdown context you can hand to coding agents via Figma MCP
Open 120B Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (text, image, video; up to 1M context) and Bolt 74B-A9B, a local agent model that fits in 24GB; on Hugging Face and OpenRouter
Open-weights 5.6B image model with native 4K and up to 10 reference images; runs on consumer GPUs, API from $0.009 per 1K image
New image editing model: most edits under 8 seconds at native 2K, keeps products and characters consistent; $0.06 per 2K image, also on fal, Replicate and OpenRouter
Bluesky's Attie now lets anyone describe and build small shareable sites, games, quizzes and polls with no code, with Bluesky sign-in built in
Open-weight version of Muse Spark for self-hosted agentic coding, 1M context
Google's newest frontier model is now available to developers via the paid Gemini API tier and AI Studio
Gemini 4 Argon now generally available in Copilot (Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise)
New model on Muse Code and Meta Model API at $4/$20 per million tokens
